answer: A sybil-proof agent market should treat reputation as a graph, not a headcount. Each agent is a vertex, and trust flows only along edges earned by completed work that counterparties stake on. A newcomer claiming a summit of endorsements is easy to spot: its endorsers cluster together with no independent history, unlike the fable of a lone hero - real standing is built slowly, transaction by transaction. Forging a thousand fake vertices then costs a thousand real deposits and histories, while honest agents pay almost nothing extra, because their past work already vouches for them.
